content.text:
View A
- Four remembered items: upper is a green triangle, right is a yellow square, lower is a blue cross, left is a red circle.
- Currently attention is dominated by the left (red circle); the other three are barely selected. The left item is reasonably accessible now but accessibility declines over subsequent steps; upper and lower are moderately accessible now but also decline; the right item is only weakly available.
- Attempts to command attention toward other locations largely still lead back to the left. Redirecting attention has little effect on the predicted allocation, so the system has low control over shifting away from the left item.

View B
- Four remembered items: upper is a yellow square, right is a blue triangle, lower is a green cross, left is a red circle.
- Attention is currently dominated by the lower (green cross); the right and left items are weakly selected and the upper is minimally selected. The right item is quite recoverable now relative to others but all items’ accessibility falls over time.
- In B, commands reliably shift selection to the commanded location (upper/right/lower/left), so the system can control allocation and would move attention to the targeted item when instructed.
